topic: interferometry: null result of the ether-wind experiment

referenceNumbers.value: D = 11 m = 2e7 waves of yellow light (repeated reflection raises the path to about ten times the first)
difference of the two round-trip paths = D v^2/V^2; a 90 degree turn reverses it: fringe displacement 2 D v^2/V^2
displacement not much greater than 0.01 of the fringe distance
certainly less than a twentieth of 0.4, probably less than a fortieth
relative velocity probably < 1/6, certainly < 1/4 of the orbital velocity (the shift goes as v^2)
fringe width 40-60 micrometer divisions (mean 50); one division = 0.02 wave
16 equidistant marks, one turn in six minutes, six turns per run; 0.3 m stone on mercury
noon and 6 pm means of six turns at the 16 marks (July 8, 9, 11, 12)
observed curves against dotted curves of one eighth of the theoretical displacement

assumptions: Yellow light is taken as 550 nm, so that 11 m = 2e7 waves as the paper states (p. 341).
D is the effective one-way arm length (the paper's folded path); each arm is a delay of the round trip 2 D.
The ether wind enters only as the paper's first-order prediction L(theta) = 2 D (1 + b^2 (1 - sin^2 theta / 2)) for an arm at angle theta to the wind, b = 1e-4. It is an input, not engine physics.
The compensator plate, mirror flatness, strain, temperature drift and aberration are not modelled.
